Changelog

survivalMPL 0.2-4.9005 (development)

  • entry= no longer errors on a non-uniform basis. Left truncation is only implemented for the piecewise-constant basis, so asking for any other basis together with entry= now falls back to "uniform" with a warning instead of stopping. The knot count reverts to the uniform default when it was the kernel-basis default, and the penalty order is recomputed for the new basis.
  • B-splines removed. R/basis-bsplines.R was a proof-of-concept never intended as a production basis; it is gone, along with its registration in zzz.R and its mentions in the articles. The registered bases are uniform, M-splines, Gaussian and Epanechnikov.
  • New dataset hiv. 300 simulated HIV seroconversion times with left- and right-censored observations and exact events, and no interval censoring - a clean illustration of left censoring on its own. See dev/data-raw/hiv.R.
  • melanoma regenerated. Two thirds of the sample (200 subjects) are now exact events and one third is censored: 58 interval, 23 right and 19 left censored. Previously it was 117 exact, 35 interval, 16 right and 132 left censored, i.e. dominated by left censoring. The simulation design, true coefficients and baseline hazard are unchanged; only pi_E, a1 and a2 differ. Fits on this dataset will give different numbers than in 0.2-4.9004.
  • New article Control Parameters, covering coxph_mpl.control(): the basis, the knots, the smoothing value and its automatic selection, the optimiser limits and tie handling.
  • The default tol makes the outer loop hard to satisfy. The automatic smoothing parameter selection stops when the degrees of freedom ν\nu change by less than 10 * tol, i.e. 10−610^{-6} by default, where Ma, Webb and Hudson (2024, Section 2.10) call ν\nu settled at changes of 0.5 to 1. On lung the default fit therefore runs out its 150 outer iterations and reports Convergence: NO, though its coefficients differ from a converged fit by at most a twentieth of a standard error. The examples now pass tol = 1e-05, the value the book uses throughout; the default itself is unchanged.
  • New website page Book, with the cover, DOI and citation for Ma, Webb and Hudson (2024), and a map from each article to the material it follows.
  • Right Censoring drops the control = coxph_mpl.control(...) block from its example and gains a residuals section: how to read the martingale and Cox-Snell plots, and why the index axis of both reflects the row order of lung rather than the fit.
  • Left Censoring rewritten around the new hiv dataset, with no interval censoring in sight: the fit checked against the coefficients that generated the data, the baseline hazard, and predicted survival by sharing status.
  • Interval Censoring now uses the bundled melanoma data instead of simulating them inline, and follows the book’s own example (Section 2.11): its fit call unchanged, including the automatic smoothing parameter selection, a hazard ratio table as in its Table 2.6, and the baseline hazard of its Figure 2.5.
  • Comparing coxph() and coxph_mpl() gains an instantaneous hazard comparison: the binned Breslow hazard against the smooth M-spline estimate.
  • Baseline hazard plots added to the right-censoring, left-censoring, interval-censoring and left-truncation articles.
  • Left Truncation drops its redundant control = coxph_mpl.control(basis = "uniform", n.obs = ...) blocks - "uniform" is the default and n.obs is not read by the fitting code - and its “What ignoring the truncation costs” comparison, keeping the article to the entry= fit, its baseline hazard and the basis fallback.
  • Getting Started lists the bases in the text instead of printing list_bases(), and points at the new Control Parameters article.

survivalMPL 0.2-4.9004 (development)

  • plot() legends now describe only what is drawn. plot.coxph_mpl() listed “Observed”, “Censored” and a quantile reference line in its legends, none of which the code draws: the points were never plotted and the quantile line and shaded region are commented out. The legends now show the knots and the line type marking θ̂u=0\hat\theta_u = 0, and, for the baseline function panels, the estimate and its confidence band. Panels gained vertical headroom and the legends an opaque background so they no longer sit on the curves. plot.residuals.coxph_mpl() gained the same treatment.
  • plot.coxph_mpl() gains an xlim argument for narrowing the displayed time range, which the baseline function panels need for right-skewed data where the full knot range compresses everything into the left edge. Only the display changes; the fit and the knots do not. upper.quantile is documented as having no effect, which has been true since the quantile line was disabled.
  • New vignette Left Truncation, following the profile-likelihood treatment of Bhaskaran, Liquet and Ma. It shows on the hiroshima data that ignoring delayed entry biases the dose and city coefficients upwards by 1.3 and 2.1 standard errors, and explains why entry= is restricted to the uniform basis.
  • The tutorials are regrouped into “Censoring and truncation” and “Modelling choices”. The home page now carries installation and one right-censored example, pointing at Getting Started for the rest. All seven articles share one output format (html_vignette with a table of contents) and one set of knitr defaults, use Example: ... headings, and end with a Next steps section.
  • Documentation regenerated: man/coxph_mpl.Rd had not been rebuilt after the entry= basis restriction was documented.

survivalMPL 0.2-4.9003 (development)

  • hiroshima dataset rebuilt, breaking change. It is now one row per subject (86,611 subjects), reconstructed from the RERF LSS14 grouped person-time table, rather than one pseudo-subject per grouped-table cell (53,782 rows). The pseudo-subject version was not usable for analysis: it produced a negative colon-dose coefficient for all-cause mortality, an artefact of high-dose cells having more person-years and hence a longer mean attained age. Changes for existing code:
    • entry is now the attained age at the 1950-10-01 start of follow-up, the age at which a subject actually enters the risk set, rather than a cell mean age at exposure. Age at exposure is available as the new agex column (exactly entry - 5.15, so the two are collinear).
    • dose is now in Gy, not mGy.
    • status is a per-subject death indicator (50,620 deaths), not a “any death in this cell” indicator.
    • reproduces the source table’s subjects, deaths and colon-cancer deaths exactly, and its person-years to within 0.33%.
  • entry= now requires basis = "uniform". Left truncation is implemented by differencing the cumulative basis, H(t) - H(entry), which is only correct for the piecewise-constant basis. Any other basis combined with entry= previously returned a silently wrong fit and now raises an error.
  • New vignettes Right Censoring and Left Censoring; left censoring was previously undocumented. Getting Started is now general information only: installation, the coxph_mpl() interface, response encodings, control arguments and methods, with its worked examples moved into those two articles. The pkgdown site groups the tutorials into sections.
  • The pkgdown site is now built into docs/ rather than pkgdown/. The old destination collided with pkgdown’s own source lookup: a generated pkgdown/index.md outranked the real index.md and the home page rendered its own previous output.
